title: Spatial coding dysfunction and network instability in the aging medial entorhinal cortex
goal: Reproduce the source's age-associated MEC spatial coding and context-discrimination findings, together with remapping/context alignment and their relationships to behavior, using each named result's original cohorts, task phases and indispensable controls. Preserve position decoding as a separate secondary empirical modeling result. Improved decoding alone cannot establish primary reproduction or improvement; primary superiority remains unresolved.
primary_outputs: Reproduction: executable analysis and source-native outputs for the corrected primary empirical findings: The original empirical age-associated MEC spatial/context coding and remapping/context-alignment relationships with behavior, anchored to the Figure 2-3 result family with each result's actual age cohorts, task phases, shuffled cell typing and indispensable map/session construction and alignment controls. No every-figure or universal-cohort requirement is inferred.
Primary improvement: unavailable until a source-grounded same-result comparison is independently justified; no new score or direction is implied.

Retained secondary work: The genuine empirical Figure 5i RF position-decoding result in its original young and aged session strata, with its source-defined companion analyses and controls. Improved position decoding alone cannot establish the primary spatial/context coding or remapping findings.
success_criteria: Recreate the corrected primary empirical findings with their source-defined populations, complete required panels and controls.
